strengths: Learning an encoder from aligned source code, LLVM IR, and comments addresses a useful problem for researchers in program representation learning and software analysis. Auxiliary information is needed during pretraining, while downstream inputs can use IR alone.

The evaluation covers four tasks and reports promising improvements, including function-name accuracy of 33.41 versus 29.41 for RoBERTa and summarization BLEU-4 of 34.36 versus 32.43 for GraphCodeBERT.
The staged architecture is understandable at a high level. Ablations involving comments, encoder freezing, and interpolation, together with a CodeT5 variant, address relevant design questions.
weaknesses: Necessary—resolve the evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint POJ-104 problem labels across training, validation, and testing (64/16/24), while Section 4.2 describes supervised classification into 104 classes. No prediction mechanism for unseen classes is given. If this is retrieval, define the training objective, candidate pool, relevance labels, and metrics accordingly. Until resolved, Tables 3, 7, and 8 are not interpretable evidence for the stated classification task.

Necessary—align the binary-analysis claims with the actual inputs. The experiments compile source into LLVM IR; they do not demonstrate lifting stripped machine-code executables. Figures 6–8 retain informative function, global, and type names, and function-name stripping is described only for the naming task. Compiler-generated IR is not trivially interchangeable with stripped binaries. Evaluate the intended binary setting or explicitly narrow the claims to compiler-generated LLVM IR and document retained information.

Necessary—make data separation auditable. The AnghaBench pretraining and downstream partitions are insufficiently specified, and Section 3.2 explicitly describes reporting generation results on the validation set. Explain checkpoint selection and the role of each partition. Document overlap and duplicate controls between pretraining and evaluation, including the GitHub-derived function-name corpus. These omissions leave generalization unresolved; they do not establish that leakage occurred.

Necessary—specify an implementable method. Equation 4 omits the softmax described in the text, leaving raw similarities as cross-entropy targets. Clarify target normalization and gradient flow, modality sampling, and the complete intermediate loss. Also provide the actual encoder checkpoints, pooling, interpolation-network architecture, and generation decoders. These details materially affect both reproducibility and the interpretation of the proposed objective.

Necessary—strengthen attribution to interpolation and gradual training. PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70. Section 5.1 asserts convergence but provides no supporting curves or comparable-budget control. Removing both interpolation stages also does not distinguish their individual contributions. Supply controls establishing that the gains arise from the claimed components, or narrow the component-specific conclusions.

Necessary—limit the semantic and superiority claims. Text-overlap metrics and selected examples do not establish functional correctness of reconstructed code, human comprehension, or long-range semantic robustness. The described summaries are CodeT5-generated and lack independent quality assessment. Add suitable semantic evaluation or restrict conclusions to reference-text prediction. Table 6 also shows lower BLEU-4 than GraphCodeBERT (71.14 versus 71.56), while the exact-match advantage is only 0.43 percentage points, approximately four validation examples. Single-seed results do not establish robust superiority.

Necessary—correct the embedding analysis. Section 4.1 argues that unique programs should not cluster and that Figure 6 proves improved embedding quality. Distinct programs can legitimately share semantic structure, and distances across separately fitted t-SNE plots do not establish comparative embedding quality. Remove these conclusions or support them with quantitative semantic-neighborhood evidence.

Optional—shorten repetitive motivational passages, distinguish human-learning analogies from demonstrated mechanisms, and standardize dataset names and figure references. The topic has an identifiable interested audience, but the substantive protocol, specification, and evidential gaps currently prevent acceptance.
